statement: Standard 10% resistor values follow the E12 series per decade; any computed resistance should be rounded to the nearest value in the target series before it appears in a schematic.
condition: Choosing any commercial resistor value at 10% tolerance.

source.book: IEC 60063 (standard); Introductory Circuit Analysis 14th ed., Table 3.5

statement: Standard 5% resistor values follow the E24 series per decade (E12 plus intermediate steps).
condition: Choosing any commercial resistor value at 5% tolerance — the default for generic design.

source.book: IEC 60063 (standard); Introductory Circuit Analysis 14th ed., Table 3.5; Sedra/Smith Microelectronic Circuits 7th ed., Appendix J

statement: The series current-limit resistor for an LED is R = (Vsupply − Vf) / If, rounded UP to the next standard E-series value so the current stays at or below the target. Typical Vf: red ≈ 1.8–2.0 V, green/yellow ≈ 2.0–2.2 V, blue/white ≈ 3.0–3.4 V; typical indicator If: 2–20 mA.
condition: Any LED driven from a fixed supply rail through a resistor.

source.book: basic circuit law (Ohm/KVL); worked examples in Practical Electronics for Inventors Ch.5 and Fundamentals of Electric Circuits
